parsed.rationale: All six records are `type-alias-object` declarations with empty `fields_or_signature` lists, meaning the structural similarity is purely that each file defines a zero-member type alias — almost certainly a SwiftUI `@main` app entry-point alias (e.g., `typealias WatchXYC = …`). Each alias carries a distinct name (`WXUISampleApp`, `WallpaperSampleApp`, `PlayerHeaderViewApp`, `PlayerHeaderViewSampleApp`, `WatchXYC`, `WXYCTVApp`) scoped to its own package (`WXUI`, `Wallpaper`, `PlayerHeaderView`, `app:WatchXYC`, `app:WXYC TV`), and the aliases exist to satisfy per-target `@main` requirements that are inherently non-shareable across app and sample-app targets. The `shared_field_count: 1` with `differing_slots: null` and `jaccard: null` confirms the overlap is structural shape only, not shared domain logic. Extracting or merging these would violate Swift's one-`@main`-per-module rule and couple unrelated app targets.
